mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Vito 109-119 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vito 109-119 CDI engine replacement typically costs between £1,500 and £4,500 depending on engine code (OM651.940, OM651.955 or OM651.958), condition type, and whether fitting is included. Rebuilt OM651.940 (109-113 CDI): £1,500-£3,300 supply only. Rebuilt OM651.955 (116-119 CDI): £1,800-£4,200 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £800-£2,500 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,200 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM651 timing chain rattle on cold start in a Vito 109-119 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 timing chain rattle is caused by tensioner seal failure allowing oil pressure loss, leading to chain stretch and guide wear. The chain is at the rear of the engine - most repairs require engine removal. REC-005099 recall addresses tensioner seal leaks on 2014 Vito models. Cold-start rattling indicates chain elongation requiring full engine-out replacement. Rebuilt OM651 units include updated tensioner seals and hardened guide rails as standard.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector seal failure on a Vito 109-119 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651's injector seals typically show warning signs before complete failure. Loss of power and rough idle. Diesel pooling in the valve cover around injectors. Increased oil consumption and sludge buildup. Check engine light with rail pressure error codes. Hard starting when warm.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my Vito 109-119 CDI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner on OM651, injector seals, EGR cooler, AdBlue injector). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. OM651 timing chain replacement: £1,200-£1,800 - do this if rattle is persistent. Injector seal & EGR replacement: £800-£1,400 - catch it early. Full OM651 rebuild: £2,500-£4,200 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Given Vito 109-119 CDI values (£4,000-£15,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my Vito 109-119 CDI has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. Vito 109 CDI: OM651.940 (95hp). Vito 110 CDI: OM651.940 (95hp). Vito 113 CDI: OM651.940 (136hp). Vito 116 CDI: OM651.955 (163hp). Vito 119 CDI: OM651.955 or OM651.958 (190hp).

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used Vito 109-119 CDI engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a Vito 109-119 CDI. The OM651's rear-mounted timing chain and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Engine must be removed to access rear timing chain - requires proper lifting equipment. Subframe must be lowered on W447 models - not a driveway job. ECU coding and injector calibration require Mercedes-Benz Star Diagnosis tools. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,200 - worth every penny.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Vito 109-119 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Vito 109-119 CDI range relies on the OM651 2.1-litre diesel - a robust commercial workhorse that has developed a well-documented reputation for specific, predictable failures. Timing chain tensioner seal failure (REC-005099) dominates replacement demand, while injector seal blow-by and EGR cooler cracking also drive significant repair enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common Vito 109-119 CDI engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Vito 109-119 CDI Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The OM651 timing chain is located at the rear of the engine block. A faulty tensioner seal (REC-005099 recall) allows oil pressure loss, causing chain slack and a characteristic rattle on cold start. The chain stretches and guides wear over time. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, leading to catastrophic valve and piston interference.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner and seal only - engine-in-situ
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught very early with no chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine-out replacement of chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if rattle is persistent or chain has stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with upgraded tensioner, new timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped or guides have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W639 or W447 Vito 109-119 CDI is worth £4,000-£15,000 depending on age and mileage - the full replacement cost of £2,500-£4,200 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £4,000, evaluate repair options carefully.
problems.recommendation: We recommend replacing the chain assembly only if cold-start rattle is recent and cylinder compression remains stable. On a Vito with confirmed chain jump, metallic knocking, or diagnostic timing deviation codes, a rebuilt OM651 is the only economically sound choice given the extensive labour required for engine-out diagnostics and the high risk of repeat failure with stock components.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 engine prices for your Mercedes Vito 109-119 CDI

problems.group: OM651 Injector Seal Blow-By & Carbon Buildup
problems.h4: OM651 Injector Seal Blow-By & Carbon Buildup - Why the Vito 109-119 CDI Loses Power
problems.rootCause: Degrading injector copper seals allow combustion gases into the crankcase, carbonising pistons and oil rings. Early piezo injectors can also fail, causing rough idle and rail pressure errors. EGR coolers crack under thermal stress, allowing coolant to enter the exhaust system.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Injector Seals & EGR Cooler Swap
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seal replacement, upgraded cooler installation, engine oil flush
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before ring damage or severe overheating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors with later magnetic type, code to ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Required if piezo injector failure or multiple seals failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete supply & fit, updated seals, tested EGR/coolant systems, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Guaranteed resolution; eliminates hidden cylinder wall scoring and turbo contamination

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a Vito worth £4,000-£15,000, injector seal and EGR replacement at £800-£1,400 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if compression loss or bottom-end damage is present.
problems.recommendation: We recommend a full reconditioned engine if compression drops below specification across any cylinder or if coolant contamination has already damaged turbocharger bearings. Partial fixes on a heavily carbon-damaged OM651 rarely survive commercial delivery cycles, making a complete rebuilt unit the most cost-effective long-term investment for fleet operators.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM651 EGR & injector-related Vito 109-119 CDI engine failure

problems.h4: OM651 DPF & AdBlue System Failures - Why the Vito 109-119 CDI Triggers Emissions Warnings
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Vito 109-119 CDI (2014-present, OM651.958 BlueTEC with AdBlue)
problems.rootCause: DPF blockage occurs on vehicles used primarily for short journeys where regeneration cycles cannot complete. AdBlue injector crystallisation blocks the dosing system, triggering countdown warnings. Low-pressure EGR valve clogging reduces power and triggers limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Forced DPF regeneration, EGR valve cleaning, reset adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative; should be performed regularly on urban-driven vans

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue injector, flush system, reset SCR counter
repairOptions.longevity: Required if crystallisation has damaged the dosing module

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with new emissions components, DPF professionally cleaned
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary for persistent emissions failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a Vito worth £4,000-£15,000, AdBlue injector replacement at £500-£800 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if emissions system failure has caused secondary damage.
problems.recommendation: For a Vito used primarily for urban delivery, regular forced DPF regenerations and EGR cleaning are essential preventative maintenance. If you're facing a third emissions component failure within 12 months, price up a full rebuilt engine - the labour to repeatedly access the SCR system becomes uneconomical.
